context: Sakura attends a small library book lending event.
purpose: Writer participating in community literacy event.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: さくらさん、本、皆に渡してくれて。
lines.en: Sakura, thank you for handing out the books to everyone.
lines.style: Warm, genuinely grateful. Soft opening. Affirming tone—noticing the effort without making Sakura self-conscious. Steady, unhurried pace.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 熱心な読者、ようけ訪ねてくれましたね。
lines.en: So many passionate readers came by. It was wonderful.
lines.style: Modest, understated pride. Speaking with quiet sincerity—not performing humility but genuine. Slight lift at the end, like she's still processing the turnout.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 本屋にない、図書、見つけられた人も。
lines.en: Even people who couldn't find it at the bookstore came to the library to see it.
lines.style: Soft amazement woven through. Gentle observation—not making a big claim, just stating what happened. Warm, conversational pace. Slight trailing-off, like reflecting aloud.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 質問にも、丁寧に答えるよう、努めました。
lines.en: I tried to answer everyone's questions carefully—gave it my full attention.
lines.style: Earnest understatement. Quiet pride held in check. Steady, grounded delivery. The sound of someone who actually showed up for people. No apology in the voice.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 長年の活動、実を結ぶね。
lines.en: All those years of doing this work—it's really bearing fruit now.
lines.style: Tender, observational. Soft wonder at seeing a pattern pay off. Slow, deliberate pace. The voice of someone who watches carefully and speaks when it matters.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.en: I want to keep going like this.
lines.style: Quiet conviction. Not pleading or seeking permission—a statement of intent. Warm but steady. The kind of thing said after thinking it through.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.en: I'll be cheering for you. Always.
lines.style: Steady, unwavering warmth. Words spoken slowly enough to land. The voice of a teacher who means exactly what she says and will remember it. Slight breath before 'always'—like a quiet promise.
